=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/orchestrate_lib.py:cmd_check_wave_status (~2454-2456) | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The documented fail-closed empty-string sentinel for `--integration-ahead-by` reaches the parser and crashes `cmd_check_wave_status` instead of forcing `project_complete=false`.
  WHY: deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro explicitly disputed this as a bug, but the other three reviewers all reported that empty-string input can still reach an `int()`-style conversion path and raise `ValueError` before the fail-closed branch runs.
- tests/test_orchestrate_integration_ahead_by_gate.py:21 | severity=medium | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: This pytest-based regression test is not runnable under the repo’s plain `python3 tests/<file>.py` CI pattern and is omitted from the unit-test allowlists.
  WHY: The file imports `pytest`, uses `tmp_path` fixtures, has no `main()` entry point, and is absent from the three workflow test allowlists, so it gets zero CI execution coverage.
- scripts/validate_editor_audit.sh:89-97 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The awk extractor only stops at `PR comment audit:`, so a future summary-format change can leak later section headings into the audit arithmetic pipeline.
  WHY: The prior inlined version exited on any generic section heading, and the shared helper now risks rc=2 false positives (`unparseable audit line`) if another heading appears before `PR comment audit:`.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:~12917-12920 | severity=low | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: The noop-suspicious recovery sweep checks the PR base ref for `orchestrator/project-*`, so orchestrator integration PRs targeting `main` are not excluded by that guard.
  WHY: The documented intent is to skip orchestrator-managed branches, but this check only filters one side of the orchestrator flow and can miss integration→default merge PRs.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

- requirement: "Ensure the shared audit helper remains compatible with future editor-summary format changes"
  expected_change_site: scripts/validate_editor_audit.sh / validate_editor_audit_arithmetic awk block
  confidence=4
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_6-plus, x-ai_grok-4_20]

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- tests/test_orchestrate_integration_ahead_by_gate.py:line 21 (import pytest), entire file (603 lines, no main() entry point) | severity=...
  PROBLEM: This test file imports pytest and uses pytest fixtures, but the repo CI runs tests via `python3 tests/<file>.py` directly without installing pytest.
  WHY: The file has no `main()` entry point and is not referenced in any of the three workflow unit-test allowlists, so it never runs in CI.
- scripts/validate_editor_audit.sh:lines 89-92 | severity=...
  PROBLEM: The awk extraction terminates only on the literal `PR comment audit:` heading instead of the more defensive generic section-heading boundary used before.
  WHY: If any new section appears between `Review file issue audit:` and `PR comment audit:`, the helper can read past the intended block and feed heading lines into the audit arithmetic parser, causing false-positive audit failures.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:lines ~12917-12920 | severity=...
  PROBLEM: The noop-suspicious recovery sweep skips orchestrator branches with `[[ "${N_BASE}" == orchestrator/project-* ]]`, but that checks the PR base ref instead of the head ref.
  WHY: Orchestrator integration PRs targeting `main` would not be excluded by this guard, so the sweep could interfere with the orchestrator merge cadence.
- Requirement: "Automated forward-merge of stable into main failed due to merge conflicts. Resolve the conflicts and merge this PR so the bug fix on stable is also present on main."
  Expected change site: All 14 conflicted files listed in the PR description
  Evidence of absence: I have inspected the PR diff across all 14 conflicting files. No merge conflict markers (`<<<<<<<`, `=======`, `>>>>>>>`) remain. The stable-side changes are present in the diff, and the forward-merge appears complete.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
